```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", message = FALSE)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Yeung_2025_indomethacin_ivh"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.70251>
* Structural PK model: Krzyzanski W et al. (2023), <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.12881>

Yeung 2025 relates model-predicted indomethacin exposure to three outcomes in
preterm neonates from two US neonatal intensive care units: prevention of
severe intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH), closure of a patent ductus
arteriosus (PDA), and renal toxicity measured as the urine output (UOP) rate
nadir within 12 h of a dose. Exposure came from the indomethacin population
PK (IND popPK) model of Krzyzanski 2023 with its CYP2C9 genotype covariate
removed, re-estimated separately on each site's data (supplement Table S2).
The paper contributes five models, packaged as five files:

| Model | What it is |
|-------|-----------|
| `Yeung_2025_indomethacin_cmh` | CYP2C9-reduced popPK, re-estimated on the Children's Mercy Hospital (CMH) dataset (plasma, dried blood spot and urine) |
| `Yeung_2025_indomethacin_vumc` | CYP2C9-reduced popPK, re-estimated on the Vanderbilt (VUMC) dried-blood-spot dataset |
| `Yeung_2025_indomethacin_ivh` | Logistic regression for severe IVH (Table 2) |
| `Yeung_2025_indomethacin_pda` | Mixed-effects logistic regression for PDA treatment failure (Table 2) |
| `Yeung_2025_indomethacin_uop` | Linear mixed-effects model for the ln UOP rate nadir (Table 2, Figure 4) |

The three regressions take exposure as a covariate column (`AUC_INDO`,
`AUC_INDO_COURSE`, `CMAX`); the two PK models are how that column is
produced.

# Population

Eighty-three neonates contributed (Yeung 2025 Table 1). The CMH cohort (45
infants given 0.1 mg/kg IV q24h x3 for IVH prophylaxis, 18 treated for PDA
with 0.1 mg/kg q12h x3 per course, 10 in both) had a median weight of 760 g
and gestational age of 26.1 weeks for the IVH group. The VUMC cohort (30
infants, < 28 weeks and < 1000 g) received a single 0.2 mg/kg dose at about
12 h of life; median weight 645 g, gestational age 24.9 weeks. Renal toxicity
was measured at CMH only. Per-model details are in each file's `population`
metadata, e.g.
`readModelDb("Yeung_2025_indomethacin_vumc")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| One-compartment IV bolus; `d/dt(urine) = CLR * Cc` | -- | Krzyzanski 2023 Equations 1-3 (structure retained by Yeung 2025 Methods 'PopPK Modeling') |
| Power PNA effect, centred on 1.25 days | -- | Krzyzanski 2023 Equation 5 and Results ('PNAmean = 1.25 days') |
| Log-scale residual, separate DBS variance | -- | Krzyzanski 2023 Equations 7-8 |
| CMH: V, CLR, CLH | 0.435 L, 0.0000172 L/h, 0.000647 L/h | Table S2, CMH column |
| CMH: PNA exponents on CLR, CLH | -0.192, 0.901 | Table S2, CMH column |
| CMH: IIV V, CLR, CLH | 38.5%, 69.0%, 215.4% | Table S2 (IIV% = 100 sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1)) |
| CMH: residual variances plasma, DBS, urine | 0.0978, 0.272, 0.0964 | Table S2 |
| VUMC: V, CLH, PNA exponent on CLH | 0.164 L, 0.000572 L/h, 1.21 | Table S2, VUMC column |
| VUMC: IIV V, CLH; DBS residual variance | 26.3%, 69.8%; 0.181 | Table S2, VUMC column |
| VUMC: renal, plasma and urine terms | fixed at CMH values | Table S2 footnote ('fixing all renal clearance ... and urine terms') |
| IVH logit: intercept, AUC, site, GA, PNA, sex, race | 14.5, -0.0005, -1.79, -0.66, 0.087, -0.78, +0.91 | Table 2, IVH block (race sign: see Assumptions) |
| PDA logit: intercept, AUCcourse, GA, PNA, condition, sex, race | 2.79, -0.0065, -0.23, 0.009, 0.24, 2.35, 0.99 | Table 2, PDA block |
| ln UOP nadir: intercept, Cmax | 1.23, -0.088 | Table 2, UOP block |
| ln UOP nadir: fluid intake | 0.0034 per mL/kg/day | Table 2, UOP block (see Assumptions) |
| ln UOP nadir: total SD | 0.53 | Back-solved from the Results text (see the Figure 4 section) |

# PK models: individual exposure

Postnatal age (PNA) is time-varying in both PK models, so the event table
carries PNA on every record. Doses are absolute amounts (mg/kg times
weight). Each cohort uses the site's median weight and postnatal age at the
first dose (Table 1) with 200 simulated infants.

```{r pk-sim}
make_cohort <- function(n, wt, pna0_h, dose_mgkg, n_dose, tau, site, id0 = 0) {
  obs_t <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 24, by = 0.5), seq(24, 504, by = 4))))
  dose_t <- (seq_len(n_dose) - 1) * tau
  one <- bind_rows(
    data.frame(time = dose_t, evid = 1, amt = dose_mgkg * wt),
    data.frame(time = obs_t, evid = 0, amt = 0)
  ) |>
    arrange(time, desc(evid))
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = id0 + seq_len(n), one) |>
    mutate(
      cmt = "central",
      # The models have two endpoints (Cc, Aurine); dvid = 1 selects Cc.
      dvid = ifelse(evid == 0, 1L, NA_integer_),
      PNA = (pna0_h + time) / 24 / 30.4375,
      SAMPLE_DBS = 0,
      site = site,
      dose_course = dose_mgkg * n_dose
    )
}

ev_cmh <- make_cohort(200, wt = 0.760, pna0_h = 5.5, dose_mgkg = 0.1,
                      n_dose = 3, tau = 24, site = "CMH")
ev_vumc <- make_cohort(200, wt = 0.645, pna0_h = 13, dose_mgkg = 0.2,
                       n_dose = 1, tau = 24, site = "VUMC", id0 = 1000)

mod_cmh <- readModelDb("Yeung_2025_indomethacin_cmh")
mod_vumc <- readModelDb("Yeung_2025_indomethacin_vumc")

rxode2::rxSetSeed(20251)
sim_cmh <- rxSolve(mod_cmh, ev_cmh, returnType = "data.frame",
                   keep = c("site", "dose_course"))
sim_vumc <- rxSolve(mod_vumc, ev_vumc, returnType = "data.frame",
                    keep = c("site", "dose_course"))
sim_pk <- bind_rows(sim_cmh, sim_vumc)

typ_cmh <- rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_cmh), filter(ev_cmh, id == 1),
                   returnType = "data.frame", keep = "site")
typ_vumc <- rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_vumc), filter(ev_vumc, id == 1001),
                    returnType = "data.frame", keep = "site")
typ_pk <- bind_rows(typ_cmh, typ_vumc)
```

```{r pk-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
pk_band <- sim_pk |>
  filter(time <= 168) |>
  group_by(site, time) |>
  summarise(
    lo = quantile(Cc, 0.05), med = median(Cc), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ggplot(pk_band, aes(time, med)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.25) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_line(data = filter(typ_pk, time <= 168), aes(y = Cc), linetype = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~site) +
  labs(x = "Time after first dose (h)", y = "Indomethacin plasma (ug/mL)",
       caption = paste("Median and 90% interval of 200 simulated infants per",
                       "site; dashed = typical value."))
```

## Dose-normalised AUC0-inf (Figure 2)

Yeung 2025 Figure 2 plots the popPK-predicted AUC0-inf divided by the total
course dose (0.3 mg/kg at CMH, 0.2 mg/kg at VUMC). The medians read from the
figure are about 230 (CMH) and 360 (VUMC) ug*h/mL per mg/kg, pooling the two
outcome groups at each site.

```{r pknca}
conc_obj <- PKNCAconc(
  sim_pk |> filter(!is.na(Cc)) |> select(id, time, Cc, site),
  Cc ~ time | site + id
)
dose_obj <- PKNCAdose(
  bind_rows(ev_cmh, ev_vumc) |> filter(evid == 1) |>
    select(id, time, amt, site),
  amt ~ time | site + id
)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, aucinf.obs = TRUE, cmax = TRUE,
                        half.life = TRUE)
nca_res <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

course_dose <- bind_rows(ev_cmh, ev_vumc) |> distinct(id, dose_course)
auc_dn <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "aucinf.obs") |>
  left_join(course_dose, by = "id") |>
  mutate(PPORRES = PPORRES / dose_course)

reference_fig2 <- data.frame(site = c("CMH", "VUMC"),
                             aucinf.obs = c(230, 360))
tbl <- ncaComparisonTable(
  auc_dn |> select(site, PPTESTCD, PPORRES),
  reference_fig2,
  by = "site",
  units = c(aucinf.obs = "ug*h/mL per mg/kg")
)
knitr::kable(tbl, caption = paste("Simulated vs Figure 2 median",
                                  "dose-normalised AUC0-inf."))
```

```{r pknca-check}
med_dn <- auc_dn |> group_by(site) |> summarise(med = median(PPORRES))
ratio <- med_dn$med / reference_fig2$aucinf.obs[match(med_dn$site, reference_fig2$site)]
ratio
# A transcription error in V or CLH (units, a dropped digit) moves the median
# several-fold; the band allows for cohort covariates fixed at site medians
# and for reading medians off a figure.
stopifnot(all(ratio > 0.67), all(ratio < 1.5))
```

The VUMC median reproduces the figure closely. The CMH median is higher than
the figure because the simulation gives every infant the median postnatal age
at first dose (5.5 h) and the nominal 0.1 mg/kg dose, while the real cohort
spans 0.23-53.7 h and 0.085-0.40 mg/kg; older infants clear the drug faster
and pull the observed median down.

Clearance matures quickly with postnatal age (exponent 0.901 at CMH, 1.21 at
VUMC), so elimination accelerates over the profile. At the CMH centring age
of 1.25 days the typical half-life is ln(2) x 0.435 / (0.0000172 + 0.000647)
= 454 h, while the terminal half-life PKNCA estimates from the last days of
the three-week window, when the infants are weeks old, is far shorter:

```{r halflife}
as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "half.life") |>
  group_by(site) |>
  summarise(median_half_life_h = median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

# Severe IVH (Table 2, Table 3)

The IVH logistic model as printed in Table 2 includes all six screened
covariates. Only gestational age is significant (odds ratio
`r round(exp(-0.66), 3)` per week). The figure below shows the predicted
probability of severe IVH across gestational age for a male, Black CMH infant
at a dose-normalised AUC of 230 and a postnatal age at first dose of 5.5 h,
with the observed proportions of Table 3 ("our study with indomethacin") for
reference.

```{r ivh, warning = FALSE}
# The regression models carry no between-subject variance (none, or a
# zero-variance random intercept), so rxode2's warning that a multi-subject
# solve has no omega is expected here and in the PDA and UOP chunks.
mod_ivh <- readModelDb("Yeung_2025_indomethacin_ivh")
ga_grid <- seq(23, 30, by = 0.25)
ivh_dat <- data.frame(
  id = seq_along(ga_grid), time = 0, evid = 0, GA = ga_grid,
  AUC_INDO = 230, STUDY_VUMC = 0, PNA = 5.5 / 24 / 30.4375,
  SEXF = 0, RACE_BLACK = 1
)
ivh_pred <- rxSolve(mod_ivh, ivh_dat, returnType = "data.frame")

# Closed-form check: the model's per-week odds ratio equals exp(-0.66).
odds <- with(ivh_pred, prob_ivh_severe / (1 - prob_ivh_severe))
or_week <- odds[ga_grid == 27] / odds[ga_grid == 26]
stopifnot(abs(or_week - exp(-0.66)) < 1e-6)

tab3 <- data.frame(GA = c(23.5, 25.5, 27.5, 29.5),
                   observed = c(2 / 13, 5 / 32, 2 / 24, 0 / 6))
```

```{r ivh-plot, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4}
ggplot(ivh_pred, aes(GA, prob_ivh_severe)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data = tab3, aes(GA, observed), shape = 1, size = 3) +
  labs(x = "Gestational age (weeks)", y = "P(severe IVH)",
       caption = "Line: Table 2 model. Circles: Table 3 observed proportions.")
```

Table 3's "probability of increased severity" column comes from a refit with
gestational age as the only covariate, whose intercept and slope are not
printed, so it is not reproduced here.

# PDA treatment failure (Table 2)

No covariate in the PDA model is significant. The subject random intercept's
variance is not reported, so it is held at zero and the model returns the
population-average logit. The predicted probability over the AUCcourse range
of Figure 3, for a male, Black infant of 26 weeks gestational age at a
postnatal age of 11 days without prior IVH prophylaxis:

```{r pda, fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4, warning = FALSE}
mod_pda <- readModelDb("Yeung_2025_indomethacin_pda")
auc_grid <- seq(0, 170, by = 5)
pda_dat <- data.frame(
  id = seq_along(auc_grid), time = 0, evid = 0, AUC_INDO_COURSE = auc_grid,
  GA = 26, PNA = 11 / 30.4375, PRIOR_INDO = 0, SEXF = 0, RACE_BLACK = 1
)
pda_pred <- rxSolve(mod_pda, pda_dat, returnType = "data.frame")
stopifnot(abs(diff(range(qlogis(pda_pred$prob_pda_failure))) -
                0.0065 * 170) < 1e-6)
ggplot(pda_pred, aes(AUC_INDO_COURSE, prob_pda_failure)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "AUCcourse (ug*h/mL)", y = "P(PDA treatment failure)")
```

# Renal toxicity (Figure 4)

Yeung 2025 simulated 1000 infants at each Cmax from 0 to 30 ug/mL with the
fluid-intake covariate at its median, including between-subject and residual
variability, and reported that the median UOP nadir falls below 1 and 0.5
mL/kg/h at Cmax 14 and 22 ug/mL, and the 5th percentile at 5 and 12 ug/mL.
Neither variance of the mixed model is printed. A single draw per simulated
infant depends only on their sum, and the four printed 5th-percentile
crossings bound its square root to 0.527-0.534 on the ln scale; the model
carries 0.53, all in the residual term. Figure 4's 90% band is about +/- 0.85
around the median on the ln scale, i.e. 1.645 x 0.52, consistent with this.

```{r uop-sim, warning = FALSE}
mod_uop <- readModelDb("Yeung_2025_indomethacin_uop")
cmax_grid <- 0:30
uop_dat <- tidyr::expand_grid(cmax = cmax_grid, rep = 1:200) |>
  mutate(id = row_number(), time = 0, evid = 0, CMAX = cmax,
         WT = 0.8, FLUID_IN_24H = 150 * 0.8) |>
  select(id, time, evid, CMAX, WT, FLUID_IN_24H)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20254)
uop_sim <- rxSolve(mod_uop, uop_dat, returnType = "data.frame")

uop_sum <- uop_sim |>
  group_by(CMAX) |>
  summarise(med = median(sim), p05 = quantile(sim, 0.05),
            p95 = quantile(sim, 0.95), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r uop-plot, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, warning = FALSE}
uop_typ <- rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_uop),
                   uop_dat |> distinct(CMAX, .keep_all = TRUE),
                   returnType = "data.frame")
ggplot(uop_sum, aes(CMAX)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = log(p05)), colour = "firebrick") +
  geom_line(aes(y = log(p95)), colour = "firebrick") +
  geom_line(data = uop_typ, aes(y = log(urine_output_nadir)),
            colour = "steelblue") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = log(0.5), linetype = 3) +
  labs(x = "Cmax per dose (ug/mL)", y = "ln UOP rate nadir within 12 h",
       caption = paste("Replicates Figure 4 of Yeung 2025: median (blue) and",
                       "5th/95th percentiles (red) of 200 simulated infants per",
                       "Cmax; dashed 1 and dotted 0.5 mL/kg/h."))
```

The threshold crossings come from the model's own parameters in closed form
(the median is the typical value; the 5th percentile shifts it by
qnorm(0.05) x 0.53):

```{r uop-check}
p <- rxode2::rxode(mod_uop)$theta
med_ln <- p[["lurine_output_nadir"]] + p[["e_cmax_urine_output_nadir"]] * cmax_grid
p05_ln <- med_ln + qnorm(0.05) * p[["expSd_urine_output_nadir"]]
crossings <- c(
  median_below_1 = min(cmax_grid[med_ln < 0]),
  median_below_0.5 = min(cmax_grid[med_ln < log(0.5)]),
  p05_below_1 = min(cmax_grid[p05_ln < 0]),
  p05_below_0.5 = min(cmax_grid[p05_ln < log(0.5)])
)
crossings
stopifnot(identical(unname(crossings), c(14L, 22L, 5L, 12L)))
# 8.4% lower nadir per 1 ug/mL (Results).
stopifnot(abs((1 - exp(p[["e_cmax_urine_output_nadir"]])) * 100 - 8.4) < 0.05)
```

The two median crossings test the printed intercept and Cmax slope
independently of the variability; the two 5th-percentile crossings only
confirm the back-solved SD.

The model-predicted per-dose Cmax in the simulated CMH cohort sits in the
same low range as the observed points of Figure 4 (almost all below 5
ug/mL), far from the toxic thresholds:

```{r cmax-range}
as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "cmax") |>
  group_by(site) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES), p95 = quantile(PPORRES, 0.95)) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Simulated Cmax (ug/mL) over the course.")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Two Table 2 cells contradict their own confidence intervals.** Every
  other row of Table 2 has its estimate inside its 95% CI and a p-value
  consistent with the CI width, so each defect is isolated to one cell.
  - *Race in the IVH model* is printed -0.91 with 95% CI (-0.67, 2.74). The
    CI excludes the estimate; it is consistent with +0.91 (mildly skewed
    profile interval, Wald p about 0.29 against the printed 0.28). The model
    uses +0.91 (non-Black vs Black). Correcting the CI instead would need two
    cells changed and their order swapped.
  - *Fluid intake in the renal model* is printed 0.00034 (mL/kg/h) with 95%
    CI (0.00068, 0.0061) and p = 0.014. The CI midpoint is 0.0034, and
    0.0034 with the CI half-width gives z = 2.46, p = 0.014, matching the
    printed p; keeping 0.00034 would need both CI bounds wrong. The unit is
    taken as mL/kg/day: Methods define the covariate as the weight-normalised
    fluid volume over the 24 h after the dose, Table 1 reports that intake in
    mL/kg/day (median 150, range 64.5-227.7), and only that scale gives a
    standard error of the observed size for a covariate spread of a few tens
    of units. The model forms the covariate as `FLUID_IN_24H / WT - 150`.
    At the median intake it is zero, so Figure 4 does not depend on it.
* **Variance of the renal model.** Not printed; 0.53 is the total SD
  back-solved from the Results text (see the Figure 4 section). The subject
  random intercept is held at zero and all variability is residual, which
  is exact for one observation per infant but ignores within-infant
  correlation across doses.
* **PDA random intercept** variance is not reported; held at zero.
* **IVH and PDA models are as printed in Table 2.** Methods describe
  backward stepwise selection, so the tabulated coefficients are the
  multivariable fits before non-significant covariates were removed. The
  reduced IVH model (gestational age only) used for Table 3 is not printed.
  The Results text quotes the gestational-age slope as -0.67 while Table 2
  prints -0.66; the table value is used.
* **VUMC renal, plasma and urine terms.** Table S2 prints NA for them and the
  footnote says they were held fixed; they are carried at the CMH
  re-estimate values (renal clearance and its PNA exponent and IIV, plasma
  and urine residual variances) and marked `fixed()`. The footnote also
  lists "dried blood spot terms" as fixed while printing an estimated DBS
  residual variance (0.181, RSE 23.9%); the estimate is used.
* **PNA centring.** Yeung 2025 retained the Krzyzanski 2023 structure without
  restating the centring value; 1.25 days (the development cohort's mean
  postnatal age at first dose) is used for both re-estimates.
* **CMH subject count.** The popPK re-estimate used the CMH development
  dataset, whose size Yeung 2025 does not restate; the CMH file records the
  38 infants of the Krzyzanski 2023 development cohort.
* **Exposure provenance.** The PDA AUCcourse and renal Cmax were derived in
  the paper from the full IND popPK model with the CYP2C9 covariate
  (Krzyzanski 2023), not from either CYP2C9-reduced model here.
* **Simulation cohorts** use each site's median weight and postnatal age at
  first dose, nominal doses and plasma sampling.
